name: FL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 14 points
Fine holds a massive money edge, with $3.7 million in outside support versus about $326,000 raised by Yonce
Prediction markets price Fine's win chance near 95 percent
No public general-election polling; Yonce has only about $34,000 in cash on hand
model.rationale: A strongly Republican-leaning district, Fine's overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and prediction markets pricing him near 95 percent all point to an incumbent win. With no public polls available, the forecast rests on fundamentals and market pricing, making the size of the margin the main uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Fine below 50 percent, or a surge of Democratic outside spending against him, would be the clearest sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Fine, the Republican incumbent, is seeking a full term in a Florida district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. He enters the fall with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $4.3 million and drawn about $3.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Eric Yonce has raised about $326,000 with limited cash on hand. A Libertarian and an independent are also on the ballot but have raised little.

No public polls of the general election are available, and no expert rating organizations have listed the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Fine roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong Republican lean, the incumbent's money advantage, and market pricing points to a comfortable Fine victory, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
